claim_traces.claim_title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
claim_traces.claim_text: "Humans only use 10% of their brain capacity — the other 90% remains dormant and untapped."
reasoning_steps: The claim that humans use only 10% of their brains is a well-known, widely debunked neurological myth
Brain imaging technologies such as fMRI and PET scans demonstrate that virtually all parts of the brain are active and have specific functions, even during simple tasks or sleep

Furthermore, evolutionary biology and clinical neurology show that unused brain areas would degenerate or atrophy over time; even minor damage to small regions of the brain often results in noticeable cognitive, sensory, or motor deficits
Neuroscientists widely agree that there is no large, dormant 90% portion of the brain waiting to be unlocked.
